records.context: ``margin`` and ``least_confidence`` are the same ranking on two classes. For C = 2, ``1 − (p₁ − p₂) = 2·min(p, 1−p) = 2·(1 − max p)``: a linear transform, so identical order and identical ties. They are not two independent choices on a binary screen — they differ only from three classes up, where ``margin`` looks at the top *two* classes while ``least_confidence`` looks only at the top one and ``entropy`` looks at the whole distribution.

records.context: ``n`` **is the number of rows the matrix actually contains**, and the supports sum to it. A row whose true class the head has no column for is counted as an error rather than dropped: the matrix grows to hold it, and the missing column stays empty because the head can never predict that class. Reporting ``n`` over one population and ``accuracy`` over another is the one thing a model card must not do — a three-class held-out set scored by a binary head used to report a perfect score on a set the model got two of three right, and the ``accuracy == trace / total`` invariant still checked out because the row was missing from both sides of it.

records.context: **The pyramid.** ``levels=1`` writes level 0 alone; more builds each level by halving the two fastest-varying space axes of the one above with a 2x **block mean** (``downsample="mean"``) or by **striding** (``downsample="stride"``). Neither is a Gaussian pyramid — there is no pre-filter beyond the box — and the block mean is the default because striding aliases: a one-pixel-wide bright structure survives or vanishes with the parity of its coordinate, so the same object appears and disappears as a user zooms. **Label and mask arrays must use** ``downsample="stride"``: the mean of labels 3 and 5 is 4, which is a different object, and averaging a boolean mask invents half-membership. Levels shrink by ``ceil(n / 2)``, so nothing is cropped off an odd edge.
records.label: spacr.ome_zarr.write_ome_zarr#2
records.source: **The pyramid.** ``levels=1`` writes level 0 alone; more builds each level by halving the two fastest-varying space axes of the one above with a 2x **block mean** (``downsample="mean"``) or by **striding** (``downsample="stride"``). Neither is a Gaussian pyramid — there is no pre-filter beyond the box — and the block mean is the default because striding aliases: a one-pixel-wide bright structure survives or vanishes with the parity of its coordinate, so the same object appears and disappears as a user zooms. **Label and mask arrays must use** ``downsample="stride"``: the mean of labels 3 and 5 is 4, which is a different object, and averaging a boolean mask invents half-membership. Levels shrink by ``ceil(n / 2)``, so nothing is cropped off an odd edge.
records.translation: **Pýramídinn.** ``levels=1`` skrifar aðeins stig 0; fleiri stig eru byggð þannig að hvert stig helmingar þá tvo rúmása stigsins fyrir ofan sem breytast hraðast, annaðhvort með 2x **blokkameðaltali** (``downsample="mean"``) eða með **skrefúrtaki** (``downsample="stride"``). Hvorugt er Gauss-pýramídi — engin forsía er umfram blokkina sjálfa — og blokkameðaltal er sjálfgefið því skrefúrtak veldur speglun: björt bygging sem er einn díll á breidd lifir af eða hverfur eftir því hvort hnit hennar er slétt eða oddatala, svo sami hlutur birtist og hverfur þegar notandi þysjar. **Merkja- og maskafylki verða að nota** ``downsample="stride"``: meðaltal merkjanna 3 og 5 er 4, sem er annar hlutur, og að taka meðaltal af booleskum maska býr til hálfa aðild. Stigin minnka um ``ceil(n / 2)``, svo ekkert er skorið af oddatölubrún.

records.context: This module is called ``spacr/omero.py`` and does not shadow the third-party ``omero`` package. Absolute imports have been the default since Python 3, so a module inside the ``spacr`` package that asks for ``omero`` gets the top-level distribution, not its own sibling. That is verified rather than assumed — see ``tests/test_omero.py::test_spacr_omero_does_not_shadow_the_third_party_package``, which puts a decoy ``omero`` package on ``sys.path`` and checks which one arrives — because a self-import here would be silent and would look like a broken OMERO install.

records.context: Returning exactly ``False`` stops the sweep and returns the rows completed so far; anything else (including ``None``) continues.  This exists for one reason: a sweep is minutes long and a GUI has to be able to show where it is and to stop it without killing the independent execution path.  Between points is the only safe granularity — one fit is atomic — so a cancel is honoured after the fit in flight, not during it.  The callback executes on the calling independent execution path, inline; it must not block, and a callback that raises aborts the sweep rather than being swallowed, because a broken progress reporter is a bug in the caller and hiding it would leave the sweep executing with nothing watching it.
records.label: spacr.power_model.scan_parameters#14
records.source: Returning exactly ``False`` stops the sweep and returns the rows completed so far; anything else (including ``None``) continues.  This exists for one reason: a sweep is minutes long and a GUI has to be able to show where it is and to stop it without killing the thread.  Between points is the only safe granularity — one fit is atomic — so a cancel is honoured after the fit in flight, not during it.  The callback runs on the calling thread, inline; it must not block, and a callback that raises aborts the sweep rather than being swallowed, because a broken progress reporter is a bug in the caller and hiding it would leave the sweep running with nothing watching it.
records.translation: Að skila nákvæmlega ``False`` stöðvar yfirferðina og skilar þeim röðum sem þegar er lokið; allt annað (þar með talið ``None``) heldur áfram. Þetta er til af einni ástæðu: yfirferð tekur mínútur og GUI þarf að geta sýnt hvar hún er stödd og stöðvað hana án þess að drepa sjálfstæða keyrsluleið. Á milli punkta er eina örugga kornastærðin — ein mátun er ódeilanleg — svo hætt er við eftir mátunina sem er í gangi, ekki á meðan hún stendur yfir. Svarfallið keyrir í línu á kallandi sjálfstæðri keyrsluleið; það má ekki stífla, og svarfall sem kastar villu stöðvar yfirferðina í stað þess að villan sé gleypt, því bilaður framvindutilkynnir er villa hjá kallandanum og að fela hana myndi láta yfirferðina ganga áfram án þess að nokkur fylgist með.

records.context: ``clear RAM`` Drops spaCR's own caches: the merged-microscope field of view LRU (:func:`spacr.crops.clear_field_cache` — by far the largest, whole image stacks), the file-format and DB-format caches, the zoomed-animation cache, the icon and preview ``lru_cache``\ s, the filter-kind cache, every live :class:`~spacr.qt.crop_thumbs.CropThumbnails` thumbnail LRU, and Qt's own ``QPixmapCache``. A process with no live Qt application also runs ``gc.collect()``. The GUI deliberately does not: walking a heap of live Qt wrappers can enter already-retired C++ objects and crash the process. It cannot return memory the allocator has decided to keep, and it says so when the measured RSS does not move.

records.context: ``worker.finished`` **is relayed through a signal into a bound method.** PySide6 delivers a plain closure connected to a worker's signal as a *direct* call on the background execution unit, and the completion handler here fills a QPlainTextEdit and a QTableWidget. records.context: It is spelt ``_rowid_``, and that is load-bearing. Every spaCR object table declares a column called ``rowID`` — the laboratory microplate row, ``'r1'``, ``'r2'`` — and SQLite identifiers are case-insensitive, so a bare ``rowid`` resolves to *that column* rather than to the row id. The version this replaces asked for ``max(rowid)`` and got two things wrong at once on every real measurements database: it scanned the whole table to take the maximum of a text column (measured: 21 ms warm, 41 ms cold, on a 200 000-row table — precisely the ``COUNT(*)`` cost this method exists to avoid), and then ``int('r16')`` raised ``ValueError``, which is not a ``sqlite3.Error`` and so escaped the caller's handler into the Qt event loop. :mod:`spacr.predictions`, :mod:`spacr.foreign` and :mod:`spacr.data_manager` all carry a comment about this shadowing; this method had not got the memo.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.column_picker.SchemaReader.estimate_rows#2
records.source: It is spelt ``_rowid_``, and that is load-bearing. Every spaCR object table declares a column called ``rowID`` — the plate row, ``'r1'``, ``'r2'`` — and SQLite identifiers are case-insensitive, so a bare ``rowid`` resolves to *that column* rather than to the row id. The version this replaces asked for ``max(rowid)`` and got two things wrong at once on every real measurements database: it scanned the whole table to take the maximum of a text column (measured: 21 ms warm, 41 ms cold, on a 200 000-row table — precisely the ``COUNT(*)`` cost this method exists to avoid), and then ``int('r16')`` raised ``ValueError``, which is not a ``sqlite3.Error`` and so escaped the caller's handler into the Qt event loop. :mod:`spacr.predictions`, :mod:`spacr.foreign` and :mod:`spacr.data_manager` all carry a comment about this shadowing; this method had not got the memo.
records.translation: Það er stafað ``_rowid_``, og á því veltur allt. Hver hlutatafla spaCR skilgreinir dálk sem heitir ``rowID`` — röð plötunnar, ``'r1'``, ``'r2'`` — og SQLite-auðkenni gera ekki greinarmun á há- og lágstöfum, svo stakt ``rowid`` vísar á *þann dálk* en ekki á raðauðkennið. Útgáfan sem þetta leysir af hólmi bað um ``max(rowid)`` og gerði tvennt rangt í einu í hverjum raunverulegum mæligagnagrunni: hún skannaði alla töfluna til að finna hámark textadálks (mælt: 21 ms heitt, 41 ms kalt, á töflu með 200 000 röðum — nákvæmlega sá ``COUNT(*)``-kostnaður sem þessi aðferð er til að forðast), og síðan kastaði ``int('r16')`` ``ValueError``, sem er ekki ``sqlite3.Error`` og slapp því framhjá villumeðhöndlara kallandans inn í atburðalykkju Qt. :mod:`spacr.predictions`, :mod:`spacr.foreign` og :mod:`spacr.data_manager` hafa öll athugasemd um þessa skyggingu; þessi aðferð hafði ekki fengið skilaboðin.

That is a 42% difference in the width of the published interval, which is not cosmetic.

records.source: :data:`CI_WALD` — asymptotic, from the covariance matrix ``curve_fit`` returns, with a t quantile on ``n - 4`` degrees of freedom. Not a normal quantile: eight concentrations with no replicates leaves 4 df, where ``t = 2.776`` against ``z = 1.960``. records.translation: :data:`CI_WALD` — nálgunarbil, reiknað út frá samdreifnifylkinu sem ``curve_fit`` skilar, með t-hlutfallsmarki á ``n - 4`` frígráðum. Ekki hlutfallsmark normaldreifingar: átta styrkleikar án endurtekninga skilja eftir 4 df, þar sem ``t = 2.776`` á móti ``z = 1.960``. Það munar 42% á breidd birta bilsins, og það er ekki bara útlitsatriði.

records.context: 1. **The curve is incomplete** — one plateau was never reached, or the midpoint sits outside the tested range. Then the EC50 is an extrapolation. :attr:`DoseResponseResult.ec50` is ``None`` in that case and the number lives in :attr:`DoseResponseResult.ec50_unconstrained`, under a name that cannot be mistaken for a result; :attr:`DoseResponseResult.ec50_bounded` is ``False`` and :meth:`DoseResponseResult.bound_statement` gives the one-sided fact the experiment does support ("EC50 > 30 µM, the highest concentration tested"). Three independent detectors have to agree it is fine before a number is released: the fitted midpoint inside the tested dose range, the observed responses bracketing the fitted half-maximum, and neither fitted plateau more than :data:`PLATEAU_SLACK` of the observed response span outside the observed responses. 2. **The data is not monotone.** A bell shape — the classic being cytotoxicity killing the signal at the top dose — is not a 4PL, and a 4PL fitted to it returns a confident EC50 for a curve of the wrong shape. Detected from the concentration-ordered per-dose medians and **refused**, with the concentrations where it turns named in the message. See :func:`monotonicity`. 3. **There is not enough experiment.** Four parameters need at least four distinct concentrations (:data:`MIN_DOSES`) and, to say anything about uncertainty, more observations than parameters (:data:`MIN_OBSERVATIONS`). A constant response has no curve in it. A **zero concentration is not an error** — a vehicle control is normal and belongs in the file — so it is excluded from the fit deliberately, counted, and reported as a reference response, never fed to ``log10``. A *negative* concentration has no such reading and is refused.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.dose_response#23

Three independent detectors have to agree it is fine before a number is released: the fitted midpoint inside the tested dose range, the observed responses bracketing the fitted half-maximum, and neither fitted plateau more than :data:`PLATEAU_SLACK` of the observed response span outside the observed responses. 2. **The data is not monotone.** A bell shape — the classic being cytotoxicity killing the signal at the top dose — is not a 4PL, and a 4PL fitted to it returns a confident EC50 for a curve of the wrong shape. Detected from the concentration-ordered per-dose medians and **refused**, with the concentrations where it turns named in the message. See :func:`monotonicity`. 3. **There is not enough experiment.** Four parameters need at least four distinct concentrations (:data:`MIN_DOSES`) and, to say anything about uncertainty, more observations than parameters (:data:`MIN_OBSERVATIONS`). A constant response has no curve in it. A **zero concentration is not an error** — a vehicle control is normal and belongs in the file — so it is excluded from the fit deliberately, counted, and reported as a reference response, never fed to ``log10``. A *negative* concentration has no such reading and is refused.
records.translation: 1. **Ferillinn er ófullgerður** — öðru hvoru flatlendinu var aldrei náð, eða miðpunkturinn liggur utan prófaða bilsins. Þá er EC50 útreikningur út fyrir gögnin. :attr:`DoseResponseResult.ec50` er ``None`` í því tilfelli og talan er geymd í :attr:`DoseResponseResult.ec50_unconstrained`, undir nafni sem ekki er hægt að rugla saman við niðurstöðu; :attr:`DoseResponseResult.ec50_bounded` er ``False`` og :meth:`DoseResponseResult.bound_statement` gefur þá einhliða staðreynd sem tilraunin styður í raun ("EC50 > 30 µM, hæsti styrkur sem prófaður var"). Þrír óháðir nemar þurfa að vera sammála um að allt sé í lagi áður en tala er gefin út: mátaði miðpunkturinn innan prófaða skammtabilsins, mældu svörin beggja vegna mátaða hálfhámarksins, og hvorugt mátaða flatlendið meira en :data:`PLATEAU_SLACK` af spönn mældu svaranna utan við mældu svörin. 2. **Gögnin eru ekki einhalla.** Bjöllulögun — klassíska dæmið er frumueituráhrif sem drepa merkið við hæsta skammtinn — er ekki 4PL, og 4PL sem mátað er að henni skilar öruggu EC50 fyrir feril af rangri lögun. Þetta er greint út frá miðgildum hvers skammts í röð eftir styrk og því **hafnað**, og styrkirnir þar sem ferillinn snýst eru nefndir í skilaboðunum. Sjá :func:`monotonicity`. 3. **Tilraunin er ekki nógu umfangsmikil.** Fjórir stikar þurfa að minnsta kosti fjóra ólíka styrki (:data:`MIN_DOSES`) og, til að segja eitthvað um óvissu, fleiri mælingar en stika (:data:`MIN_OBSERVATIONS`). Fast svar felur engan feril í sér. **Styrkur núll er ekki villa** — leysisviðmið er eðlilegt og á heima í skránni — svo það er vísvitandi útilokað frá mátuninni, talið og tilkynnt sem viðmiðunarsvar, en aldrei sent í ``log10``. *Neikvæður* styrkur hefur enga slíka túlkun og er hafnað.

records.context: Why this shape is what lets an arbitrary organelle count land. The number of organelles a processing session may declare is not fixed. In a flat vocabulary each new organelle is twenty new settings that every tooltip table and translation catalog has to learn; here it is one COLUMN, and the number of questions does not move. :meth:`ObjectSettingsGrid.add_object` is that operation, and it starts a new organelle from the first one's answers rather than from a global default nobody chose.
records.label: spacr.qt.widgets.object_settings_grid#3
records.source: WHY THIS SHAPE IS WHAT LETS AN ARBITRARY ORGANELLE COUNT LAND. The number of organelles a run may declare is not fixed. In a flat vocabulary each new organelle is twenty new settings that every tooltip table and translation catalog has to learn; here it is one COLUMN, and the number of questions does not move. :meth:`ObjectSettingsGrid.add_object` is that operation, and it starts a new organelle from the first one's answers rather than from a global default nobody chose.
records.translation: Hvers vegna það er einmitt þessi lögun sem leyfir hvaða fjölda frumulíffæra sem er. Fjöldi frumulíffæra sem vinnslulota má skilgreina er ekki fastur. Í flötum orðaforða er hvert nýtt frumulíffæri tuttugu nýjar stillingar sem hver ábendingatafla og hver þýðingaskrá þarf að læra; hér er það einn COLUMN (dálkur), og fjöldi spurninga breytist ekki. :meth:`ObjectSettingsGrid.add_object` er sú aðgerð, og hún byrjar nýtt frumulíffæri út frá svörum þess fyrsta en ekki út frá almennu sjálfgefnu gildi sem enginn valdi.

records.context: **Isolation forest requires** ``contamination`` — the share of the data that is bad — declared *in advance*. That share is precisely the unknown the analysis is trying to estimate. records.context: **A column with no values at all comes back as** ``object``. This is the common one and it is not a data problem: ``pandas.read_sql`` builds the frame from the rows it gets, so a column that is ``NULL`` in every row arrives as a column of ``None`` and pandas types that ``object`` -- even though SQLite declares it ``REAL``. spaCR writes ``NULL`` for an honest NaN, and whole measurements are legitimately NaN for a whole database: ``skew_intensity``/``kurtosis_intensity`` are NaN for every uniform object, and ``mode_intensity`` was NaN for every object in every database written before the SciPy shim in ``measure._extended_regionprops_table``. Such a column is converted to ``float64`` NaN, which is what it always meant. Nothing is lost, so nothing is warned about -- and the caller's own all-NaN filter then drops it and says so.
records.label: spacr.schema.coerce_model_feature_types#1
records.source: **A column with no values at all comes back as** ``object``. This is the common one and it is not a data problem: ``pandas.read_sql`` builds the frame from the rows it gets, so a column that is ``NULL`` in every row arrives as a column of ``None`` and pandas types that ``object`` -- even though SQLite declares it ``REAL``. spaCR writes ``NULL`` for an honest NaN, and whole measurements are legitimately NaN for a whole database: ``skew_intensity``/``kurtosis_intensity`` are NaN for every uniform object, and ``mode_intensity`` was NaN for every object in every database written before the SciPy shim in ``measure._extended_regionprops_table``. Such a column is converted to ``float64`` NaN, which is what it always meant. Nothing is lost, so nothing is warned about -- and the caller's own all-NaN filter then drops it and says so.
records.translation: **Dálkur sem hefur alls engin gildi kemur til baka sem** ``object``. Þetta er algengasta tilvikið og það er ekki gagnavandamál: ``pandas.read_sql`` byggir rammann úr þeim röðum sem það fær, svo dálkur sem er ``NULL`` í hverri röð berst sem dálkur af ``None`` og pandas gefur honum tegundina ``object`` -- jafnvel þótt SQLite skilgreini hann sem ``REAL``. spaCR skrifar ``NULL`` fyrir raunverulegt NaN, og heilar mælingar eru réttilega NaN í heilum gagnagrunni: ``skew_intensity``/``kurtosis_intensity`` eru NaN fyrir hvern einsleitan hlut, og ``mode_intensity`` var NaN fyrir hvern hlut í hverjum gagnagrunni sem skrifaður var áður en SciPy-millilagið kom í ``measure._extended_regionprops_table``. Slíkum dálki er breytt í ``float64`` NaN, sem er það sem hann merkti alltaf. Ekkert glatast, svo ekki er varað við neinu -- og sía kallandans sjálfs fyrir dálka sem eru eingöngu NaN fjarlægir hann síðan og segir frá því.
